categories.main_business_segments: Jabil operates through three primary business segments: Regulated Industries, Intelligent Infrastructure, and Connected Living and Digital Commerce. Regulated Industries focuses on automotive and transportation, healthcare and packaging, and renewables and energy infrastructure. Intelligent Infrastructure serves capital equipment, cloud and data center infrastructure, and networking and communications. Connected Living and Digital Commerce targets digitalization and automation, including warehouse automation, robotics, and digital commerce industries.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Jabil leverages highly automated, continuous flow manufacturing, advanced electronic and mechanical design, and integrated supply chain management. Its production methods include in-line assembly, computerized control and monitoring, electronic supply chain management, and advanced test and verification systems. The company invests in R&D for automation, next-generation electronic interconnections, advanced materials, optical and sensor integration, and sustainable manufacturing solutions.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Jabil serves a diverse customer base, primarily large, technology-driven companies in high-growth industries. Its key markets include automotive, healthcare, packaging, renewables, cloud and data center infrastructure, networking, communications, warehouse automation, robotics, and digital commerce. In fiscal 2025, its five largest customers accounted for 36% of net revenue, with 87 customers representing about 90% of net revenue.
categories.geographic_coverage: Jabil operates globally with approximately 100 locations in 30 countries, including major manufacturing sites in China, Malaysia, Mexico, and the United States. About 75% of its fiscal 2025 revenue was generated from foreign sources, with significant operations and assets in Asia, the Americas, and Europe. Its global footprint enables local-for-local and regional manufacturing to serve customers efficiently worldwide.
categories.supply_chain_position: Jabil operates as a contract manufacturer and supply chain solutions provider, primarily in the downstream segment of the supply chain. It manages the entire product lifecycle from design and engineering to manufacturing, assembly, and direct-order fulfillment, acting as an outsourced manufacturing partner for its customers. The company also provides procurement, logistics, and supply chain orchestration services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Jabil's strategic priorities include expanding long-term customer relationships, diversifying its product and customer portfolio, leveraging its global manufacturing footprint, and investing in value-added services and design expertise. Its R&D initiatives focus on automation, advanced materials, next-generation electronics, optical and sensor technologies, sustainable design, and AI-driven supply chain solutions. The company also pursues strategic acquisitions to enhance capabilities and enter new markets.
categories.revenue_model: Jabil primarily generates revenue through turnkey manufacturing services, which include product design, production, assembly, and supply chain management, billed on a per-unit or project basis. Additional revenue streams come from value-added design services, direct-order fulfillment, configure-to-order services, and, to a lesser extent, licensing and service fees. The company also manages procurement and logistics for customers, sometimes on a net revenue basis.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Jabil competes with global electronic manufacturing services (EMS) providers such as Flex Ltd., Celestica, Hon Hai (Foxconn), Plexus, and Sanmina, as well as with customers' internal manufacturing operations. It differentiates itself through scale, advanced automation, global reach, and integrated design-to-delivery capabilities. Jabil is considered a leading EMS provider with strong positions in regulated and high-growth technology markets.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal year 2025, Jabil reported net revenue of $29.8 billion and net income of $657 million. The company has a large global workforce of 135,000 and significant assets across multiple continents. While revenue grew 3.2% year-over-year, the company experienced a decrease in net income due to product mix and restructuring charges, but maintains a strong balance sheet and robust cash flow, with ongoing investments in growth and share repurchases.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Jabil emphasizes its ability to deliver end-to-end, customer-centric manufacturing solutions that reduce costs, accelerate time-to-market, and enhance supply chain resilience. Its differentiation lies in advanced automation, global scale, integrated design and engineering services, and digital supply chain orchestration. The company positions itself as a trusted, technologically advanced partner capable of supporting complex, regulated, and rapidly evolving markets.
